issues.legal_issue: Providing residential accommodation to a public institution’s employees can constitute use of premises for the furtherance of the institution’s activities.
material_facts: The landlord was a university that had received the building under a will and obtained probate of the will.
The university sought eviction so that the building could be used to provide residential accommodation for its employees.
The lower courts concurrently found that the university’s need for the premises was bona fide and that the building was residential in nature, although some portions had been used commercially.
issues.conclusion: The employee-housing use furthered the university’s activities, so the eviction applications fell within Section 22(d) and the eviction orders were correct. The appeals and special leave petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 permits a public institution to seek eviction notwithstanding Section 14 or any other law when the requirements in the section are met. Under Section 22(d), premises bona fide required by a public institution for the furtherance of its activities may be recovered; the Explanation includes educational institutions within ‘public institution.’ Providing residential accommodation for employees can directly further an institution’s activities because adequate housing helps employees remain contented and enables the institution to function properly. The Court stated that it was unnecessary to deal with the earlier decisions cited at the hearing.

predicates.institutional_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding is an eviction case brought by an institution against occupants of premises it owns or controls.
predicates.landlord_is_public_institution: The landlord is a public institution, including an educational institution.
predicates.premises_bona_fide_needed_for_employee_h: The institution genuinely requires the premises to provide residential accommodation for its employees.
predicates.employee_housing_supports_institutional_: Providing accommodation for the employees helps the institution operate effectively.

issues.definition: When a public institution brings an eviction proceeding and genuinely needs the premises to house employees in a way that supports its work, eviction is permitted for that institutional use.
